Below is a high-level professional workflow and a toolbox of advanced techniques—largely centered on Adobe Photoshop/Lightroom, Capture One Pro and specialist plug-ins—that many studios use to turn a “good” shot into a “wow” shot.  You can adapt these steps to Affinity Photo, DxO PhotoLab, GIMP or other platforms with equivalent tools.

1. Raw-First Workflow & Calibration  
   • RAW capture → Adobe Camera Raw (ACR), Lightroom or Capture One Pro  
     – Apply or build a calibrated camera/profile (Sony S-Log, Canon C-Log, X-Trans, etc.)  
     – Enable lens-profile corrections for distortion, vignetting and chromatic aberration  
   • Photo culling & rating → mark Keepers, generate Smart/Proxy Previews  

2. Global Tonal & Color Foundation  
   • Exposure & Contrast  
     – Adjust exposure to place most clipped highlights in a recoverable zone  
     – Use Highlights/Shadows sliders (or Zones in C1) to open up midtone detail  
   • White Balance & Tint  
     – Eyedropper on neutral tone or use custom Kelvin/Tint for mood  
   • Curves & Levels  
     – S-shaped RGB curve for contrast, individual-channel curves to correct casts  
   • Profile & Color Space  
     – Work in ProPhoto RGB/16-bit where possible, or a wide-gamut camera profile  

3. Local Adjustments & Masking  
   • Graduated/Radial Filters (LR/PS) or Layer-masks (PS)  
     – Darken/brighten skies, emphasize subjects, vignette selectively  
   • Targeted HSL / Luminance / Saturation   
     – Isolate foliage greens, skin-tone oranges, deepen blues without affecting reds  
   • Luminosity Masks (PS):  
     – Create 5-7 grayscale masks (highlights, midtones, shadows) for precision brushing  
   • Selective Color & Blend-If  
     – Refine tonal transitions via blend-if sliders or individual-color sliders  

4. Advanced Color Grading  
   • Split-Toning / Color Lookup Tables (3D LUTs)  
     – Apply subtle warm/cool split, or import a custom LUT (e.g. acquired film emulation)  
   • Channel Blending (Lab Color)  
     – Use Lab’s L-channel for contrast, “a”/“b” channels for selective color boosts  
   • Gradient Maps on Soft Light / Overlay  
     – Two- or three-point gradient map for cinematic color casts  

5. Retouching & Skin/Texture Work  
   • Frequency Separation  
     – Low-frequency layer for color/tone, high-frequency for pore/texture; blend as needed  
   • Dodge & Burn (non-destructive)  
     – 50% gray layer set to Overlay, paint with white/black at low opacity to sculpt form  
   • Healing Brush / Clone Stamp / Patch Tool  
     – Remove stray hairs, blemishes, minor distractions; work on a sample layer above  
   • Liquify & Puppet Warp  
     – Subtle shape control: face-aware liquify for portraits, puppet warp for compositional tweaks  

6. High Dynamic Range (HDR) & Exposure Blending  
   • Auto-Merge to HDR (LR/PS or Aurora HDR)  
     – Tone-map conservatively, then fine-tune in ACR or Curves  
   • Manual Exposure Blending  
     – Stack bracketed exposures as Smart Objects in PS, paint masks to reveal best-exposed areas  
   • HDR Panoramas & Focus-Stacking  
     – Merge multiple frames for ultra-wide DOF or extreme dynamic range  

7. Noise Reduction & Sharpening  
   • RAW-based Noise Reduction  
     – Luminance vs. Chrominance separation in LR/PS or DxO DeepPRIME, Topaz DeNoise AI  
   • Local Noise Control  
     – Apply selective noise reduction via masks on shadowy/underexposed regions  
   • Sharpening Workflow  
     – High Pass filter on a merged layer set to Overlay/Soft Light (use masks to target edges)  
     – Unsharp Mask / Smart Sharpen for fine-tuning; separate channels if color noise persists  

8. Lens & Perspective Correction  
   • Upright Transform (PS) or Keystone Tool (C1)  
     – Auto, Level, Vertical or Full correction; fine-tune via manual slider  
   • Adaptive Wide-Angle (PS) for curved lines  
   • Perspective Warp for architectural precision  

9. Compositing & Removal of Distractions  
   • Content-Aware Fill & Patch Tool  
     – Remove unwanted people, poles, power lines; refine with clone brushing  
   • Sky/Background Swaps  
     – Match light direction/color; use masks and edge-refinement (Select and Mask)  
   • Smart Objects & Layer Comps  
     – Preserve source edits, swap versions (before/after) easily  

10. Color Management & Final Output  
   • Soft-Proof in Photoshop (“View → Proof Setup”)  
     – Preview on target ICC profile (web sRGB, magazine CMYK, gallery print ICC)  
   • Output Sharpening & Resizing  
     – Use “Export As…” in LR or PS’s “Save for Web (Legacy)” for screen; perform print-specific sharpening  
   • Archive & Versioning  
     – Save layered .PSD/​.PSB, flattened high-res TIFF and web-optimized JPEG/PNG  

11. Optional Plug-Ins & AI Tools  
   • Nik Collection (Color Efex, Dfine), Topaz Labs (Sharpen AI, Gigapixel), LuminarAI  
   • Photoshop Neural Filters (style transfer, super zoom)  

—  
By combining a disciplined RAW-first pipeline with precise local edits (luminosity masks, dodge & burn, frequency separation) and judicious use of color grading (LUTs, split toning, Lab-channel work), you can systematically identify and neutralize elements that weaken an image’s impact—noise, uneven exposure, distracting background clutter or flat color—and replace them with targeted enhancements that elevate the final aesthetic.
